_what: 2-per-Act sample pricing the renumbering exposure before a full pass.

_population.why_this_population: these are the facts where a renumbering can make a REAL, correctly-fetched citation point at the wrong provision -- the failure mode that produced the Cap.212 reversal and the Cap.332 presumptive incident.

⚠️_what_a_clean_act_does_and_does_not_me: 2 clean draws from 20 facts is a LOWER BOUND on cleanliness, not a clearance. An Act reading clean here is NOT YET SHOWN to be a problem; it is not shown not to be.

blocked_notes.Cap.50: ✅ RESOLVED 2026-10-05 -- THE ACT WAS LOCATED AND ALL 21 FACTS CHECKED. See eval/controls/check_cap50_facts_vs_re2023.py. Two primary routes, both HTTP 200, both 773,203 bytes, 50pp, sha256 IDENTICAL: the Fund's own nssf.go.tz/uploads/publications/...NSSF ACT CAP 50 RE. 2023.pdf (listed at nssf.go.tz/publications/act) and the Attorney General's revised-acts portal at oagmis.oag.go.tz/portal/acts/revised/155/download. ⚠️ MY EARLIER 'NOT LOCATED' VERDICT WAS WRONG IN AN INSTRUCTIVE WAY. The eight hosts tried and their per-host diagnoses were all accurate -- including that nssf.go.tz's homepage links nothing matching publication|act across its 41 links, re-verified. But the CONCLUSION drawn from that was too strong: a homepage that does not link a route is NOT evidence the route does not exist. The Act sat at /publications/act, which the broken /pages/* family simply does not cover. And the oag.go.tz trail stopped one subdomain short -- revised Acts live on oagmis, not on the parent site I searched. SO 'THE ADMINISTERING BODY HOSTS ITS OWN ACT' HELD PERFECTLY; the search stopped one route and one subdomain short, which is a different failure from the pattern breaking down. Recorded that way round because the pattern is still the right thing to try first on the next Act.
blocked_notes.Cap.438: RESOLVED 2026-10-05, and the earlier BLOCKED verdict was MY ERROR, not the regulator's. tra.go.tz hosts BOTH editions: CHAPTER_438-THE_TAX_ADMINISTRATION_ACT.pdf is R.E.2019 (259,711 bytes) and Tax_Administration_Act.pdf is the current OAG compilation (945,982 bytes, 88pp). The project ALREADY cited the current one -- paye_penalty_rate's verified_by has quoted s.89(2) from it since 2026-09-02. I picked the stale URL out of a grep of recorded paths without checking which fact cited which, then recorded the whole Act as unverifiable. So 'the regulator serves its own Act at a stale edition' was half right at best: it serves both, and the actionable fact is that one of OUR recorded URLs is the old one (deliberately, for the two EFD facts that quote the 2019 wording and name the renumbering explicitly).
